newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany not seeking stronger EMU criteria -Stark.
newsitem.headline: Germany not seeking stronger EMU criteria -Stark.

text.p: Germany is not trying to strengthen the criteria for adopting Europe's single currency or to keep some nations out of the monetary club, Juergen Stark, state secretary in the Bonn finance ministry said on Wednesday.
Stark was speaking to a group of foreign journalists at the Federal Press Office.
"Germany is not trying to strengthen the treaty or to add criteria which will stop nations getting in to stage three," Stark said.

He was countering speculation by some observers that Germany's attempts to set up a tight stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline within European economic and montary union (EMU) is a means of making it harder for countries to qualify.

The Maastricht Treaty on EMU includes a set of fiscal targets for European Union members hoping to adopt the single currency. They include restriction of budget deficits and public debt. The participants in EMU in 1999 will be chosen based on which countries meet the targets in 1997.
Stark said all the elements of the proposed stability pact had their basis in the Maastricht Treaty. "You cannot argue that we are operating outside the treaty," he said.
